name: scroll-chapters
title: Scroll chapters
author: Eduardo Retana
description: Chapters with a sticky index. A total bar follows scroll(); each chapter's bar follows its own named view-timeline through timeline-scope. Pure CSS.

meta.descriptionEs: Índice fijo con una barra total por scroll() y una barra por capítulo con view-timeline con nombre y timeline-scope. CSS puro; sin soporte, el índice es una lista de enlaces.

api.name: chapters
api.description: id is the anchor and names the chapter's timeline (--retana-chapter-<id>), so it must be unique on the page.

api.name: loading / error / labels / motion
api.description: Skeleton, alert, nav label and copy, and a still mode that hides the bars.

docs: Idea from Midudev's scroll-driven animations demo (reel, 2026). Technical reference: MDN, CSS scroll-driven animations. Implementation is Retana UI's own; no code from the reel. Pure CSS with a local <style>: no JavaScript, no client boundary, safe in a Server Component. The animation sits inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and @supports (animation-timeline: …), and animation-timeline comes after the animation shorthand. Without support or with reduced motion the content is visible and still. Pass motion="off" to hold it still from a toggle. Baseline 2026 newly available (27 Oct 2026): Chrome and Edge 115+, Safari 26+, Firefox 159+. The item ships no theme, cssVars, or fixed colors. Loading and error are host states: the piece renders a skeleton or an alert. The total bar uses scroll(nearest block), so it follows the page or the nearest scroller. Chapter bars use animation-range contain 0% contain 100% and animate transform scaleX only. Bars are aria-hidden; the index links are real anchors.
